c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: What does a variable actually do in this program?

A.text: It holds a number for the motor block to use

B.text: It makes the car go faster on its own

C.text: It stores the program on the micro:bit

c1.why: A variable is a box with a number in it. The motor block is what moves the car — it just reads the box.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: `change speed by 1` — what does it do to a variable that already holds 40?
c2.why: `change by` adds to what is already there. `set to` is the one that throws the old value away.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: Why does the car's front wheel lift off the ground when you start it at full speed?

B.text: The speed jumps from 0 to 100 all at once

C.text: The program has a bug in it

c3.why: A sudden jump in speed tips the body backwards. Climbing the speed a little at a time is the whole point of this chapter.

r1.label: Q1

A.text: Stays still — the variable never reaches the motors

B.text: Drives, then stops when speed hits 100

C.text: Drives at speed 1 the whole time

r1.why: Every trip round the loop puts a bigger number into the motors. That is what "gradually" looks like in code.

r2.label: Q2

D.text: Speed goes back to 0 and the car climbs again

r2.why: The `if` catches the value at 100 and resets it. The car speeds up, drops back, and speeds up again — forever.

r3.label: Q3

D.text: They turn once for each loop

r3.why: The number climbs, but nothing hands it to the motors. A variable on its own moves nothing.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: How is this different from climbing by 1?

A.text: It climbs past 100 and never resets

B.text: It gets to its top speed in far fewer loops

r4.why: Bigger steps mean fewer trips round the loop — so the start is harsher, which is the thing this chapter is trying to avoid.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: The car barely moves and never gets faster. What is wrong?

B.text: The forever block should be `on start`

C.text: The motor block needs two different numbers

D.text: The variable needs a different name

d1.why: `set to 1` writes 1 over and over. `change by 1` adds — that is what makes the number climb.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: The car reaches full speed and sits there for a long time before it drops back. Why does the reset come so late?

B.text: Motor speed stops at 100, but the variable is checked at 150

C.text: The `if` block is in the wrong place

D.text: The variable is not allowed above 100

d2.why: The variable does climb past 100, but the motors cannot go faster than full — so the car looks stuck while it waits for 150.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Starting from the top of `forever`, in what order does this chapter's program do these? 1 add 1 to speed · 2 send speed to the motors · 3 check whether speed has hit 100
b1.why: The program drives with the number it has, then raises it, then checks it — the same order as the Plan. Other orders can work too (the wiki checks first), but this is the one we built.

b2.label: Q2
b2.why: Setting it up belongs outside the loop. Inside, it would reset the number every trip and the car would never climb.
